back: A mindset, defined by 4 values, guided by 12 principles and shown through many practices.
Individuals and interactions over processes and tools.
Working software (a working product) over comprehensive documentation.
Customer collaboration over contract negotiation.
Responding to change over following a plan.

front: Do the right-hand items of the Manifesto have value?
back: Yes. Processes, documentation, contracts and plans still have value; the left-hand items are valued more.
Satisfying the customer through early and continuous delivery of value.

front: Primary measure of progress in agile
back: A working product.
Welcome them, even late. Change is a competitive advantage for the customer.
The team works at a pace that sponsors, developers and users could keep up indefinitely.
The art of maximizing the amount of work not done.

front: Which principle is behind the retrospective?
back: At regular intervals the team reflects on how to become more effective, then tunes and adjusts its behavior.

front: Most efficient way to share information, per the agile principles
back: Face-to-face conversation.
Definable: proven procedures, low uncertainty; suits predictive. High-uncertainty (knowledge work): new design and problem-solving; suits agile.
Repeated cycles that allow feedback on unfinished work, in order to improve it. Aims at correctness.
Delivering finished pieces that the customer may be able to use immediately. Aims at speed of delivery.

front: How agile relates to iterative and incremental
back: Agile combines both: the team iterates over the product to create finished increments.

front: Typical length of an agile iteration
back: 1 to 4 weeks.
Predictive: as much as possible up front; the plan drives the work. Agile: plan a little, deliver, learn, replan.
Lean thinking is the wider family. Agile and the Kanban Method are both descended from it.
Focus on value, small batch sizes, elimination of waste.
A less prescriptive, 'start where you are' approach from lean manufacturing, adapted for knowledge work. Continuous pull, no iterations.
Doing agile: following the practices. Being agile: living the values and principles, delivering value early and adapting from feedback.
The smallest version of a product that can be built and tested quickly to check assumptions. Central to Lean Startup.
Predictive fixes scope and estimates time and cost. Agile fixes time and cost and adjusts scope to fit.
Covers many frameworks that fulfil the Manifesto's values and principles: Scrum, XP, Kanban, Crystal, FDD, DSDM.
